questions.text: What regulation governs the licensing and operational standards for funeral homes and embalming practices in the Philippines?

rationale.a: RA 7160 governs local government units; not specific to funeral homes.
rationale.c: BP 344 addresses accessibility; not specific to funeral home operations.
rationale.d: RA 10066 governs cultural heritage; not funeral service regulation.
rationale.correct: Republic Act 4167 established the Funeral Services Board and governs licensing, operational standards, and regulatory compliance for funeral homes, embalming, and related services in the Philippines. (RA 4167, Funeral Services Board)
rationale.takeaway: RA 4167 (Funeral Services Board) regulates funeral homes in the Philippines.

questions.text: A funeral home cold storage (morgue) facility is designed to accommodate 3 bodies. What is the minimum area required?

rationale.a: 4–5 sqm is too small for equipment and operational access.
rationale.c: 15–18 sqm exceeds the standard for small-facility cold storage.
rationale.d: 20–25 sqm is larger than required for 3-body capacity.
rationale.correct: Cold storage (morgue) minimum = 6–12 sqm for 2–4 body capacity. This accommodates refrigeration unit(s), access for loading/unloading, and compliance with sanitary standards. (Funeral Home Design Standards)
rationale.takeaway: Cold storage (morgue) minimum area = 6–12 sqm for 2–4 body capacity.

questions.text: What is the required temperature range for a funeral home cold storage (morgue) facility?

rationale.c: 0–2°C is near-freezing; 2–4°C is the standard refrigeration range.
rationale.d: Below 0°C (freezing) is not necessary for short-term cold storage.
rationale.correct: Cold storage for bodies requires 2–4°C (refrigeration temperature) to slow decomposition. (Funeral Home Design Standards, Mortuary Science Practice)
rationale.takeaway: Funeral home cold storage temperature = 2–4°C per industry standards.

questions.code_citation: Funeral Home Design Standards; Mortuary Science Practice

questions.text: A funeral home chapel is divided from the business office area (Group E). What minimum fire-resistance rating is required between the Group E and Group C zones per the National Building Code?

rationale.a: 30-minute rating is insufficient; NBC specifies 1-hour minimum.
rationale.c: 2-hour rating exceeds the Group E–C separation requirement.
rationale.d: 3-hour rating is more restrictive than required.
rationale.correct: PD 1096 requires 2-hr (non-sprinklered) or 1-hr (sprinklered) per Table 604/Rule VII occupancies to contain fire and protect public occupants. (NBC Fire Safety, Occupancy Separation)
rationale.takeaway: Fire separation between Group E (office) and Group C (chapel) = 1-hour minimum per NBC.

questions.text: The minimum area for an embalming room in a funeral home is approximately:

rationale.a: 6–8 sqm is insufficient for equipment and ventilation requirements.
rationale.d: 25–30 sqm exceeds typical requirements but may be used for larger facilities.
rationale.correct: Embalming room minimum = 12–20 sqm to accommodate an embalming table, chemical storage, instrument trays, separate HVAC intake/exhaust, floor drain, and sanitary fixtures. (No specific code minimum; typical practice 12 sqm+)
rationale.takeaway: Embalming room minimum area = 12–20 sqm per funeral industry standards.

questions.text: For a funeral home chapel with 300-person seating capacity, how many separate exits are required per the National Building Code?

rationale.a: 1 exit is insufficient for 300 persons; maximum 1 exit at 49 persons.
rationale.c: 3 exits are not mandated solely by seating count; 2 exits satisfy 300 persons.
rationale.d: Not all assembly venues require 4 exits; 2 exits meet the 300-person threshold.
rationale.correct: PD 1096 requires 2 exits for assembly occupancies >50 persons (Rule III Sec 1004). For a 300-person chapel, 2 exits are mandatory. Additional exits may be required if the space exceeds certain dimensions or occupancy thresholds, but 2 is the minimum. (NBC Table 3, ERR-DSGN-021 inverse)
rationale.takeaway: Chapel with 300 persons requires minimum 2 separate exits per NBC (required at 50+ persons).

questions.text: A funeral home chapel seats 300 persons. Calculate the minimum combined exit width required per PD 1096 Rule III Table III-2 (5.6-7 mm/person).

rationale.a: 1.50 m uses 5 mm/person; NBC specifies 7.6 mm/person.
rationale.b: 1.80 m uses 6 mm/person; correct standard is 7.6 mm/person.
rationale.d: 3.0 m uses 10 mm/person; exceeds the required rate.
rationale.correct: Exit width = Occupant load × 7.6 mm/person ÷ 1000 = 300 × 7.6 ÷ 1000 = 2.28 m. (NBC Table 3, ERR-DSGN-019 inverse)
rationale.takeaway: Chapel exit width = 300 persons × 7.6 mm/person ÷ 1000 = 2.28 m.

questions.text: A funeral home viewing room expects 50 simultaneous visitors. Using a density of 1.1–1.5 sqm per visitor, calculate the minimum viewing room area.

options.text: 25 sqm (50 × 0.5), which is insufficient for the expected visitor density and does not meet the minimum space requirements
45 sqm (50 × 0.9), which falls short of the recommended area for comfort and accessibility
100 sqm (50 × 2.0), providing ample space but exceeding typical requirements for such a setting

rationale.a: 25 sqm uses 0.5 sqm/person; correct standard is 1.1–1.5 sqm/person.
rationale.b: 45 sqm uses 0.9 sqm/person; below the required minimum of 1.1 sqm/person.
rationale.d: 100 sqm at 2.0 sqm/person exceeds the standard requirement.
rationale.correct: Viewing room area = Number of visitors × 1.1–1.5 sqm/person. For 50 visitors: 50 × 1.1 = 55 sqm (minimum), to 50 × 1.5 = 75 sqm (comfortable). (Funeral Home Design Standards)
rationale.takeaway: Viewing room area = 50 visitors × 1.1–1.5 sqm/person = 55–75 sqm.

questions.text: A funeral home facility contains an administrative office, reception area, viewing room, chapel, and embalming room. How should the occupancy classification be structured?

options.text: Single Group A (Residential), which is typically used for living accommodations rather than commercial or institutional facilities
Single Group C (Education and Recreation), which is not applicable as the facility does not primarily serve educational or recreational purposes
Mixed: Group D (business office, reception) + Group C (chapel)
Single Group D (Institutional), which encompasses facilities providing care or supervision, but not applicable to funeral homes

rationale.a: Group A is residential; funeral homes are commercial establishments.
rationale.b: Group C applies to the chapel, but the office/reception area is Group E mercantile.
rationale.d: Group D is institutional (hospitals, care facilities); funeral homes are commercial and assembly.
rationale.correct: A funeral home is mixed-use: the business area (office, reception) is Group D (business), and the chapel (assembly) is Group C. Each zone has separate egress requirements and fire separation standards. (NBC Mixed-Occupancy Classification)
rationale.takeaway: Funeral home classification = Group E (business area) + Group C (chapel). Separate egress and fire separation required.

questions.text: A funeral home embalming room requires a specialized HVAC system. Which is the correct design approach?

options.text: Shared HVAC with the chapel to reduce costs, which may compromise air quality and odor control
Separate negative-pressure HVAC system to prevent odor transmission to public areas
Natural ventilation through windows only, which is insufficient for maintaining necessary air quality standards
Standard commercial HVAC serving the entire building equally, which does not address specific needs of the embalming room

rationale.a: Shared HVAC allows odor/chemical transmission to chapel; separate system required.
rationale.c: Natural ventilation is insufficient for chemical handling and odor control.
rationale.d: Standard building HVAC cannot control negative pressure needed for embalming room.
rationale.correct: Embalming room HVAC must be separate and maintain negative pressure (exhaust > intake) to prevent odor and chemical vapor from migrating to public areas (chapel, viewing room). (Funeral Home Design Standards, HVAC Best Practice)
rationale.takeaway: Embalming room requires separate negative-pressure HVAC system for odor/chemical control.
